tasks.short: Run practical training sessions that work for our warehouse shifts and office teams.

today.trigger: A scheduled session, new operating procedure or recurring mistake requires instruction.
steps: Check the learning objective, audience, language needs and available session time.
Adapt slides, demonstrations and exercises to the site and job.
Deliver the session and adjust explanations when participants struggle.
Observe practice, answer questions and record follow-up needs.
drudgery: Rewriting examples for different jobs and sites
Preparing repeated explanations and exercise variations
Typing session notes and follow-up actions
today.time_sinks: Preparation and follow-up are repetitive, while demonstrations, discussion and supervised practice require the specialist's presence.

lenses.faster: Generate exercise variations, facilitator notes and follow-up drafts from an approved lesson pack. Repeated preparation and note formatting largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A confirmed session can trigger a draft facilitator pack and participant reminders. Delivery and adaptation to the group stay with the trainer.
lenses.ambitious: Give every shift short practice sessions using examples from its own work, rather than relying on occasional large classroom sessions.
lenses.joy: Remove slide rewriting and administrative follow-up. Keep demonstrations, discussion and the satisfaction of seeing someone master a task.
lenses.options: Prepare five ways to teach the same objective: demonstration, role play, team exercise, discussion and a short video script.
lenses.altitude: Design reusable teaching formats and coach supervisors to deliver them consistently across the three sites.
reach: Help HR Business Partners run supervisor workshops
Coach onboarding buddies in practical instruction
Help operations managers structure shift briefings

tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, establishing trust and spotting unsafe practical behaviour require a present, competent trainer.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can prepare and adapt teaching aids, but live instruction depends on interaction, observation and judgement.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist confirms a session brief containing its objective, audience and approved source material.
steps: Retrieve the current approved lesson and relevant site procedure from SharePoint.
Draft alternative exercises, plain-language explanations and facilitator notes.
Have the specialist select and check the pack before delivery.
Deliver practical instruction and assess understanding through human observation.
Turn the trainer's notes into a checked follow-up list and record actual attendance.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every teaching pack and conducts the session; a competent assessor confirms practical competence where required.
data_needed: Trainer observations without unnecessary personal details
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint lesson version and approval register; actual attendance in Studytube.

evidence.claim: An LLM can draft exercise alternatives and facilitator notes from supplied procedures; classroom effectiveness still needs a local pilot.
The 25% human-time saving and 1.25-times execution speed are planning assumptions, not measured Noordhaven results.

risks: Generated exercises could contradict local safety procedures; check them against the approved source.
Translations can sound fluent while changing a safety instruction; use a competent language reviewer.

A simulation or quiz does not establish safe equipment operation. Practical requirements remain relevant: [Arboportaal guidance](https://www.arboportaal.nl/onderwerpen/veiligheid-op-het-werk/arbeidsmiddelen/gebruik-van-arbeidsmiddelen).
research_questions: How much session time currently goes into preparation and follow-up rather than delivery?
Do AI-assisted packs reduce preparation time without lowering observed practical performance?
Which languages and literacy needs occur on each shift, including among agency workers?

tasks.short: Create and update training guides, handouts and online lessons from our approved procedures.

today.trigger: A new procedure, changed policy or training request requires learning materials.
steps: Find the current procedure, policy and existing lesson files.
Ask the procedure owner to resolve missing or conflicting information.
Write a guide, slides, handout and knowledge questions.
Obtain content and safety approval, then publish the materials.
drudgery: Copying the same content into several formats
Searching for the latest approved procedure
Formatting handouts and rewriting question banks
today.time_sinks: Finding authoritative content and recreating it in several formats consume more time than selecting the learning objective.

lenses.faster: Produce a guide, slide outline, quiz and facilitator notes from one approved source. Manual copying and first-draft formatting largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A newly approved SharePoint procedure version can trigger draft updates and a reviewer task. Publication follows explicit approval.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain short, current job guides for every important warehouse and transport procedure, with versions suitable for the languages actually used.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive formatting and rewriting. Spend more time testing whether employees understand and can use the instructions.
lenses.options: Generate several versions for different experience levels, languages and teaching formats, all traceable to the same source.
lenses.altitude: Own the standards, source controls and approval process for a maintained library of learning materials.
reach: Help HR Administration maintain employee policy guides
Help operations owners turn procedures into usable work instructions
Help Recruiters prepare realistic job previews

tasks.human_edge: The specialist determines what people need to learn; the procedure owner remains responsible for technical accuracy.
tasks.pattern_why: A workflow can gather approved sources, generate several outputs and run checks, but publication needs content-owner approval.

in_practice.trigger: An approved source changes or the specialist submits a material request.
steps: Check source approval, version and ownership; stop if sources conflict.
Generate draft materials with references to the supporting source sections.
Run deterministic checks for required sections, terminology and unresolved placeholders.
Route the drafts to L&D and the relevant technical or safety owner.
Publish approved versions and mark superseded materials as obsolete.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the teaching design; the designated procedure owner approves technical content and translated safety instructions before publication.
systems: Studytube authoring tool, subject to licence validation
data_needed: Approved source documents and version identifiers
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint source-to-material register with draft, approval and publication versions; Studytube published lesson record.

evidence.claim: Studytube documents an authoring tool that can generate training content with AI from uploaded files and lets users review and edit the result.
Automatic source-change detection, approval routing and the proposed savings require a Noordhaven-specific implementation and pilot.

risks: An outdated source can produce convincing but incorrect materials; require approved versions and named owners.
Generated questions may reward memorisation rather than practical understanding.
External provider materials may have reuse restrictions.
Uploaded files require approved processing terms, access controls and retention under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven's Studytube licence include the documented AI authoring capability?
Are approved procedures consistently versioned and assigned to an owner in SharePoint?
What percentage of drafts pass technical review without substantial correction?
Does review and maintenance effort leave a net saving after several procedure updates?

tasks.short: Provide the right refresher and skills training for each job, site and shift.

today.trigger: A certificate approaches expiry, a manager reports a skill gap or an employee changes duties.
steps: Check the role requirements, training history and reported skill gap.
Choose a suitable course or practical session.
Arrange places, shift release and agency coordination where needed.
Deliver or commission training and confirm completion and practical follow-up.
drudgery: Checking expiry lists and training histories
today.time_sinks: Roster coordination and individual follow-up are repeated across three sites, especially during seasonal hiring.

lenses.faster: Use an approved role-to-training matrix to identify requirements and prepare booking options. Repeated record checking and reminder drafting shrink.
lenses.autonomous: Deterministic rules can flag expiry dates and assign established refresher requirements. Exceptions and changes to training pathways go to L&D.
lenses.ambitious: Offer short follow-up practice after training so skills stay useful on the job, including for seasonal agency workers.
lenses.joy: Remove expiry chasing and repetitive booking administration. Keep coaching, demonstrations and discussions about development.
lenses.options: Compare an external course, an internal practical session and a blended refresher against the same competence requirement.
lenses.altitude: Maintain reliable job-based training pathways and a supervisor coaching system.
reach: Help HR Business Partners structure development conversations
Help operations managers maintain training coverage
Help HR Administration coordinate agency-worker training records

tasks.human_edge: L&D and the supervisor distinguish a genuine skill gap from unclear instructions, equipment problems or insufficient practice.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules can handle established requirements and reminders, while selecting and delivering an effective intervention remains human-led.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled expiry check, confirmed role change or manager training request.
steps: Match workers to approved job requirements using validated employee or agency identifiers.
Flag missing evidence, approaching expiries and uncertain matches.
Prepare course and shift options with costs and available capacity.
Have L&D and the supervisor confirm the intervention and release time.
Record verified completion and arrange human practical assessment where required.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the programme; supervisors approve release time; authorised assessors confirm practical competence.
systems: Approved agency exports or validated connectors
Proposed rules service and LLM drafting assistant
data_needed: Certificate types, evidence and applicable validity dates
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube training records and a restricted SharePoint exception register.

evidence.claim: Structured requirements and expiry dates support deterministic matching; an LLM can draft options and communications around those results.
The proposed 30% saving assumes usable role, certificate and shift data and does not shorten required practical instruction.

risks: Certificate completion can be mistaken for competence or permission to perform a specific job.
Agency workers may be missing from AFAS or have duplicate identities across agencies.
Training time, costs and release arrangements need checking against the applicable CAO and agency agreements.
Nightly data cannot guarantee readiness for an immediate shift; supervisors need a current check before relevant work starts.
research_questions: How complete and accurate are role requirements and certificate validity records?
Can all three agencies supply dependable identity and training evidence?
Does administration represent enough of this task to support a 30% saving?
Do refresher interventions improve observed performance after several weeks?

tasks.short: Track training completion and check whether it improves readiness and performance through day 90.

today.trigger: A training cycle ends, a reporting deadline arrives or a manager asks whether training worked.
steps: Export enrolments, completions, feedback and assessment records.
Reconcile those records with employee, site and role data.
Calculate coverage and compare results across suitable groups.
Discuss findings with managers and recommend programme changes.
today.time_sinks: Data cleaning and report preparation crowd out discussion of whether people can actually perform their work.

lenses.faster: Automate reconciliation and metric calculations, then use an LLM to summarise redacted comments. Manual report assembly largely disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A validated refresh can update completion and coverage reports and flag missing records. Interpretations and recommendations require review.
lenses.ambitious: Measure week-one readiness and day-30 and day-90 practical progress for each onboarding cohort, rather than relying on course completion.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet cleanup and reporting repetition. Spend time investigating weak results with supervisors and employees.
lenses.options: Compare results by site, shift, job and training format with sample sizes and uncertainty shown.
lenses.altitude: Design an evaluation system that distinguishes attendance, learning, practical competence and retention.
reach: Support the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst with learning measures
Help HR Business Partners evaluate onboarding
Help the Controller assess training cost per verified outcome

tasks.human_edge: The specialist interprets operational context and challenges easy explanations for differences between groups.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations and an LLM feedback-summary step can prepare the report; a person must approve its conclusions.

in_practice.trigger: Validated training and HR extracts become available for the scheduled reporting period.
steps: Reconcile worker identifiers and quarantine unmatched or duplicate records.
Calculate fixed metrics with denominators, timestamps and data-quality checks.
Summarise redacted feedback and link each theme to supporting comments.
Prepare cohort comparisons without claiming that training caused retention changes.
Have L&D approve the interpretation and agreed improvement actions.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves conclusions; People Analytics validates metric definitions and joins before reports are used for decisions.
systems: Studytube exports or validated API access
Proposed calculation pipeline and approved LLM
data_needed: Enrolments, actual attendance and verified completions
Start dates, roles, sites and employment status
Day-90 retention and cohort eligibility definitions
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh and calculation logs; restricted SharePoint interpretation and action register.

evidence.claim: Repeatable joins and metric calculations suit deterministic software; LLMs can assist with qualitative feedback summaries.
The 55% saving and two-times speedup are untested estimates dependent on data quality.

risks: Small site or shift groups can expose individual employees; restrict access and suppress unsuitable breakdowns.
Training completion and 90-day retention do not establish productivity or causation.
New employee-monitoring arrangements can engage OR rights: [AP guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/ondernemingsraad).

AI assessment of individual learning outcomes or worker performance needs an intended-use review under the EU AI Act: [Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act).
research_questions: Can training and HR records be joined reliably, including agency workers?
What observable criteria will managers use to confirm that a new hire is productive?
Are cohort sizes sufficient for useful comparisons without exposing individuals?
Does automated reporting free time for action, or merely produce more reports?

tasks.short: Plan onboarding and training so every starter has a workable route to productive work.

today.trigger: An employee or agency worker is due to start, or a team needs a new training programme.
steps: Confirm role, site, start date and training requirements.
Build a programme with induction, practical instruction, a buddy and follow-up.
Arrange trainers, shift release, rooms and course places.
Track week-one delivery and resolve missed activities.
Review progress with the manager through day 90.
drudgery: Chasing owners and rescheduling missed activities
today.time_sinks: Repeated coordination across sites, supervisors, buddies, trainers and agencies creates delays and missed handovers.

lenses.faster: Generate a proposed programme from approved role and site templates, then check scheduling constraints automatically. Repeated copying and basic conflict checking disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A confirmed starter record can create a proposed plan, owner tasks and deadline reminders. Approved standard assignments can then run by rules.
lenses.ambitious: Provide every starter, including agency workers, with a clear day-one, week-one and day-90 pathway and named owners.
lenses.joy: Remove calendar chasing and repeated checklist creation. Keep programme design, welcoming people and solving difficult onboarding cases.
lenses.options: Compare plans for immediate starts, peak-season cohorts and staggered shift starts, showing capacity and cost constraints.
lenses.altitude: Own the onboarding operating model and improve the handovers that determine whether a hire becomes productive.
reach: Take on onboarding coordination from HR Administration
Improve Recruiter-to-HR starter handovers
Help operations managers plan buddy and trainer capacity

tasks.human_edge: L&D and managers decide what readiness means, resolve operational trade-offs and support starters who need a different approach.
tasks.pattern_why: Planning spans several systems and people; a workflow can propose and coordinate the programme after a manager approves it.

in_practice.trigger: A confirmed AFAS starter or validated agency order enters the onboarding queue.
steps: Validate identity, start date, role and site; reconcile the recruiting handover where applicable.
Apply approved onboarding requirements and identify missing evidence.
Prepare a schedule using supervisor-confirmed shifts, buddy availability and trainer capacity.
Have L&D and the manager approve the programme before issuing assignments and invitations.
Track week-one activities and escalate missed safety prerequisites.
Collect human readiness checks and review progress at agreed points through day 90.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D and the manager approve the plan; the supervisor confirms readiness before relevant operational work begins.
data_needed: Confirmed starter records and unique identifiers
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint onboarding plan and approval history; Studytube learning records.

evidence.claim: Studytube documents an AFAS integration that retrieves data each evening, with variable completion time; this does not establish a real-time starter feed.
Cross-system planning, agency coverage and the estimated savings require configuration and local validation.

risks: Late or immediate starters can be missed by nightly feeds; maintain an explicit supervisor-confirmed exception route.
Creating tasks does not ensure trainers, buddies or shift release are available.

Changes to group training arrangements can require OR consent; check CAO coverage and the proposed policy change: [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67).
Agency records need clear responsibility for access, accuracy and timely removal.
research_questions: How early do confirmed starters enter AFAS or the agency order process?
Which onboarding failures come from administration, and which come from insufficient operational capacity?
Can supervisors maintain usable shift and buddy availability data?
Does the pilot improve week-one completion and verified day-90 readiness?

tasks.short: Compare training formats for learning results, shift coverage, cost and travel.

today.trigger: A programme is being renewed, its costs rise or managers question the delivery format.
steps: Collect attendance, feedback, practical results and supplier prices.
Estimate trainer time, employee release time, travel and operational disruption.
Compare classroom, virtual, workplace and blended delivery.
Discuss trade-offs and choose a format to pilot or retain.
today.time_sinks: Comparable cost and outcome information is scattered, and employee release time is easily omitted.

lenses.faster: Extract supplier terms into a checked comparison and calculate total costs with fixed formulas. Manual spreadsheet rebuilding shrinks.
lenses.autonomous: Validated price or attendance changes can refresh scenarios. The delivery decision remains with L&D and operations.
lenses.ambitious: Test which format produces durable practical competence for each type of work instead of choosing mainly on course price.
lenses.joy: Remove offer rekeying and repetitive arithmetic. Keep designing pilots and debating worthwhile trade-offs.
lenses.options: Compare classroom, virtual, workplace and blended scenarios with sensitivity to group size, travel, paid learning time and trainer capacity.
lenses.altitude: Set evidence and cost standards for how Noordhaven chooses training delivery.
reach: Help the Controller analyse training unit costs
Support FP&A with training demand scenarios
Help operations managers compare training schedules

tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges whether a format can teach the required skill and whether workers can realistically participate.
tasks.pattern_why: Software can calculate scenarios and AI can structure offers, but pedagogical suitability and operational trade-offs require human judgement.

in_practice.trigger: L&D opens a delivery review for a defined programme and competence objective.
steps: Extract offer terms and outcome evidence, marking missing or incomparable fields.
Have L&D verify the extracted terms and assumptions.
Calculate costs, capacity and travel using versioned formulas and stated factors.
Generate several delivery scenarios with sensitivity ranges.
Choose a pilot with operations and compare practical outcomes before broader adoption.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D confirms teaching suitability, Finance checks material cost assumptions and operations approves release arrangements.
systems: Proposed approved LLM for offer extraction
data_needed: Internal trainer and employee time costs
Travel distances and documented emissions factors
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint decision file containing verified inputs, calculation version, scenarios and pilot results.

evidence.claim: Offer extraction with human verification and deterministic scenario calculations are technically plausible using supplied documents and spreadsheets.
The 50% saving assumes comparable inputs and reusable cost models; it is not a measured result.

risks: The cheapest format may provide poor practical transfer or exclude workers with limited digital access.
Omitting paid learning time, replacement cover or no-shows distorts costs.
Different cohorts can make effectiveness comparisons misleading.
Travel emissions estimates need documented boundaries and factors rather than invented precision.
research_questions: Can Finance and operations provide credible employee release and replacement costs?
Which skills require supervised physical practice regardless of delivery cost?
Are practical outcomes comparable across formats and participant groups?
Does the preferred scenario remain attractive when attendance and replacement assumptions change?

tasks.short: Keep our training approach current with useful developments in learning, safety and workplace rules.

today.trigger: A regular reading slot, professional newsletter or reported policy change.
steps: Scan publications, professional updates and relevant official guidance.
Read promising sources and check their credibility and relevance.
Record useful findings and discuss implications with colleagues.
Decide whether to update a programme or test a new approach.
drudgery: Sorting generic advice from useful evidence
Maintaining reading notes and source links
today.time_sinks: Finding a small number of relevant, reliable items requires scanning substantial unrelated material.

lenses.faster: Receive a deduplicated reading brief with source links, dates and relevance to Noordhaven. Routine scanning and note formatting shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled workflow can collect updates from an approved source list and prepare a draft digest. L&D decides which findings deserve action.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a small test programme for promising teaching methods and role-specific AI literacy, with results shared across sites.
lenses.joy: Remove newsletter clutter. Keep deeper reading, discussion and experiments that challenge the current approach.
lenses.options: For each promising finding, prepare several responses: monitor it, run a small pilot or revise a specific programme.
lenses.altitude: Set the evidence standards and research agenda that guide learning improvements.
reach: Provide HR Business Partners with checked learning briefings
Support the HR Director with training implications of policy developments
Help the HRIS Analyst identify learning-system capabilities worth testing

tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises weak evidence, understands local relevance and decides when an idea warrants operational change.
tasks.pattern_why: Collection, deduplication and draft summaries can run on a schedule; a person checks sources and approves actionable interpretations.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly schedule or a detected update from an approved official source.
steps: Collect accessible updates from official bodies, research sources and selected professional publications.
Deduplicate items and preserve source, publication date and retrieval date.
Draft summaries separating reported evidence from suggested Noordhaven implications.
Have L&D open and check shortlisted sources, referring legal questions to the appropriate adviser.
Approve a brief and record any pilot or material-update decision.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the digest and proposed actions; legal or policy interpretations need the responsible expert's review.
data_needed: Approved source list and access rights
Priority topics and current programme inventory
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint evidence register with source links, checked summaries and action owners.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, deduplication and source-linked summarisation are plausible, but source coverage and summary accuracy need testing.
The 45% saving assumes the current task contains substantial scanning; deeper reading remains necessary.

risks: Summaries can miss qualifications or treat a proposal as an enacted rule.
Vendor claims can be mistaken for independent evidence of learning effectiveness.
Collection must respect publication licences and access restrictions.

AI literacy is a relevant learning topic; its scope should follow actual tool use and roles: [European Commission AI Act overview](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
research_questions: Which sources have actually led to useful programme changes in the past year?
Does the digest find important updates without increasing false alarms?
How often does source checking materially change an AI summary?
Does time saved on scanning translate into more useful reading or experiments?

tasks.short: Check instructor materials for accuracy, clarity and fit before employees use them.

today.trigger: An instructor submits new or revised materials, or an existing course is due for review.
steps: Collect the materials, learning objectives and authoritative procedures.
Read the content for accuracy, completeness and audience suitability.
Check exercises and assessments against the required skill.
Send corrections to the instructor and review the revised version.
today.time_sinks: Routine completeness checks and revision comparisons consume time that could go into assessing teaching quality and practical relevance.

lenses.faster: Run repeatable checks automatically and receive source-linked findings with suggested corrections. Manual checklist completion and revision comparison shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A submission can trigger format checks, source comparisons and a draft review report. Acceptance follows human approval.
lenses.ambitious: Review all submitted materials consistently, including agency induction packs and small local refresher lessons that currently receive limited scrutiny.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated proofreading and comment consolidation. Keep discussing teaching quality with instructors and testing difficult explanations.
lenses.options: Offer several corrections for a weak section: clearer wording, a worked example, a practical exercise or a different assessment.
lenses.altitude: Define and calibrate the quality standard for Noordhaven's training library.
reach: Help operations owners review work instructions
Help HR Administration check policy explanations
Help HR Business Partners review manager workshop materials

tasks.human_edge: A specialist and technical owner judge whether materials teach the right behaviour safely; textual consistency alone cannot establish that.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules and source-grounded LLM review can produce most of the review report, while final acceptance remains a human decision.

in_practice.trigger: An instructor submits a versioned material pack to the review queue.
steps: Validate the submission, objectives and current approved reference sources.
Run deterministic checks for required sections, broken references and version mismatches.
Use an LLM to flag unclear explanations and possible source conflicts with supporting passages.
Prepare a prioritised review report and proposed corrections.
Have L&D and the technical owner decide acceptance, then check the corrected version.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D accepts teaching quality; the technical or safety owner signs off relevant content. Automated checks never grant final acceptance.
systems: Proposed rules checker and company-approved LLM
data_needed: Approved learning objectives and review rubric
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint review record containing findings, source references, reviewer decisions and accepted version.

evidence.claim: Deterministic document checks and source-grounded draft reviews are plausible; reliable detection of substantive safety errors requires local validation.
The 60% saving assumes many checks are repeatable and excludes automatic approval of safety-critical materials.

risks: AI can miss a serious error while flagging harmless wording differences.
A quality score can create false assurance; retain findings and explicit reviewer decisions.
Poor extraction from diagrams or scanned files can hide important content.
This estimates preparation of a review result; technical accountability and acceptance remain human.
research_questions: Against a set of previously reviewed materials, which important errors does the checker miss?
How much reviewer time is spent on repeatable checks versus specialist judgement?
Are findings traceable enough for instructors to correct materials without extra discussion?
Does revision checking reduce turnaround without increasing accepted errors?

role.altitude: The role becomes the designer and owner of Noordhaven's learning system: approved job pathways, reliable materials, capable trainers and evidence of practical readiness through day 90.
reach: Onboarding coordination currently carried by HR Administration
Learning measurement design alongside the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Supervisor coaching support alongside HR Business Partners
Training cost and capacity scenarios alongside the Controller and FP&A
Recruiting handovers and realistic job previews alongside Recruiters
Operational instruction quality alongside site procedure owners
role.ceiling_note: Today's workflows are hypotheses for this fictional company. These eight tasks total 850.1 hours per FTE annually, about 53% of the role. Applying the task estimates gives a gross capacity ceiling of about 775 hours across 2 FTE, valued at roughly EUR 53,000 annually at EUR 68/hour. This is capacity, not cash savings; overlap, setup, maintenance and additional review reduce it. Savings and speedups assume validated integrations and include review of outputs; speedups concern task execution, while shift schedules, course availability and approval waiting can still determine calendar completion. Practical instruction, trust, competence assessment and policy accountability limit automation. Keep training records within defined AVG/GDPR purposes, retention and access controls; agree OR involvement for relevant policy or monitoring changes. Re-integration learning may support the absence-to-return stream, but medical judgements and Wet verbetering poortwachter case ownership stay with the responsible professionals; exclude diagnoses from learning workflows.
skills_to_grow: Designing observable job-readiness and practical assessment criteria
Maintaining role-to-training rules and authoritative source libraries
Checking AI outputs, translations and source references
Designing integrations with identity matching, exception handling and audit records
Evaluating learning outcomes without confusing correlation with causation
Working with the OR, privacy specialists and technical owners on appropriate boundaries
Building credible training cost and capacity scenarios
role.ambitious_version: Give every employee and agency starter a clear, shift-compatible path to safe, productive work, supported by current instructions and a capable buddy. Use human readiness checks at week one and through day 90 to find and fix weak handovers, then invest released capacity in practical coaching and programmes that improve Noordhaven's share of hires who are productive and still here after 90 days.
